items.title: Dan Barrett interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: go out and buy Cole Porter songs and go out and buy George Gershwin songs you know

ctx.x: As a parting question, if you had a word of wisdom to give to students that you know will be watching this tape, students trying to make their way in the profession of jazz and understand the idiom, just a parting shot.

Yeah, I actually think I have something pertinent to say. I would advise them that in their practicing as they’re playing scales and as they’re playing exercises and trying to improve their technique, I would take about 25 or 30 percent of that time, or a margin of that practice time and use it to study songs. And go out and buy sheet music, not just lead sheets with the chord symbols, but shell out the bucks that it takes and go out and buy Cole Porter songs and go out and buy George Gershwin songs you know. And…
